previous_statement: A sound completion requires exactly one of two mathematical changes outside this proof step: (i) register an allowed validated dependency, synchronized with the same constants and witnesses, which asserts that this explicit Pi_delta is bijective (or a C^1 diffeomorphism) onto S_delta with inverse (u_delta,h_delta) and identifies its first component with the u_delta used by lem-stage1-approximate-group-laws; or (ii) weaken the root contract by deleting the explicit unique-two-component-inverse clause and retaining only the conclusions G actually exported by lem-stage1-approximate-group-laws. Without (i) or (ii), node 1 must remain unproved rather than promoting the unsupported assertion R.
new_statement: Let A,B >= 1 and k in (0,1/2] be universal witnesses from lem-stage1-approximate-group-laws, and let P >= 1 and q in (0,1/2] be universal witnesses from lem-stage1-polar-retraction. Set C_grp^0=A, C_pol^0=max(B,P), and kappa_pol^0=min(k,q). For every root instance, monotonicity of the nonnegative scalar expressions makes both external lemmas applicable. lem-stage1-polar-retraction supplies the explicit C^1 diffeomorphism Pi_delta and its unique two-component inverse (u_delta,h_delta); lem-stage1-approximate-group-laws supplies the stated C^1 operations, identities, and A*epsilon_r estimates for the first polar-inverse component, which is the same u_delta by uniqueness. Since A<=C_grp and epsilon_r>=0, those estimates weaken to C_grp*epsilon_r. Hence the arbitrary instance has every root conclusion, proving node 1.
